title: Psalm 91, shelter of the Most High; the noonday demon; angels bear you up ↔ The jinn hear the recitation

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited (weight 6.0); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 6.0); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 5.8); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Only in Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil: The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?'; Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city; What Lot says to the townsmen; How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts]; When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him; What falls from heaven on Sodom; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place; Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish; Stones of baked clay (sijjil), in layers, each marked by the Lord, rain on the town; and 3 more.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts]; God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city; The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'.

title: Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi ↔ Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven
summary: These two units share 7 motifs: a specific sign marks the moment to board, the flood waters are hot or boiling, animals taken aboard in pairs, a member of the hero's family is lost….

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A specific sign marks the moment to board (weight 6.3); The flood waters are hot or boiling (weight 6.0); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); A member of the hero's family is lost (weight 5.8); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 5.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; and 22 more.

title: Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
summary: These two units share 8 motifs: condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life', the magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes, pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks), the defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the lord of moses and aaron….

passages.note: Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life' (they also say Pharaoh compelled them to practise sorcery)
passages.text: قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ

title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains ↔ Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs
summary: These two units share 5 motifs: why pharaoh and egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts], moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts], prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign, a staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff….

passages.note: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (Pharaoh's response to the sign: Exod 7:13 wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh wə-lōʾ šāmaʿ ʾălēhem ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart hardened as God foretold (God hardens it himself at 14:4, 14:8); Q 26:49 has no hardening and no divine agency, only Pharaoh's rage: āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu la-kabīrukumu lladhī ʿallamakumu s-siḥra, with a threat of amputation and crucifixion.)
passages.text: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

passages.note: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (Why Egypt refuses: Exod 8:15 the magicians admit ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ, yet wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh ... ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart is hardened as God foretold; Q 27:14 wa-jaḥadū bihā wa-staiqanathā anfusuhum ẓulman wa-ʿuluwwan, they rejected the signs though inwardly convinced, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. Refusal by God's design becomes knowing, self-chosen denial.)
passages.text: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

passages.note: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.)
passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

passages.note: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾin ~ hāvēʾ nāʾ yādəkā bə-ḥêqekā ... wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: hand into the bosom (jayb / ḥêq) and out white. The Quran's 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ) excludes exactly what Exodus says, that the hand was leprous (məṣōraʿat), and needs no second step of restoring it (4:7).)
passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

passages.note: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign
passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

passages.note: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (into his bosom (jayb), white without evil)
passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

passages.note: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff
passages.text: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ

passages.note: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff
passages.text: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

passages.note: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest
passages.text: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ

passages.note: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest
passages.text: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ

passages.note: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (fa-lammā jāʾathum āyātunā mubṣiratan qālū hādhā siḥrun mubīnun ~ wa-yyiqrāʾ gam Parʿōh la-ḥăkhāmîm wə-la-mkhaššəfîm wa-yyaʿăśû gam hēm ... bə-lahăṭêhem kēn: Pharaoh's side treats the signs as magic; Exodus shows it by having the magicians copy them, the Quran by having Pharaoh's people call them 'clear sorcery'.)
passages.text: فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1). Pair score 28.1.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 38 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; and 2 more.

title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains ↔ The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper
summary: These two units share 7 motifs: moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the egyptian's death [divergence between the texts], moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts], aaron's role beside moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts], prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign….

In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.)

passages.note: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. title: Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs ↔ The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper
summary: These two units share 7 motifs: the thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and moses turns and flees without looking back, traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there, moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and god's response [divergence between the texts], moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts]….

Exodus then has God order him to grasp the snake by the tail (šəlaḥ yādəkā wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô); the Quran has God reassure him: yā Mūsā lā takhaf innī lā yakhāfu ladayya l-mursalūna.)
passages.text: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

title: The annunciation and the mission of Jesus ↔ Mary, the spirit in human form, the birth under the palm, the speaking infant (Surah 19:16-40)
summary: These two units share 4 motifs: mary asks how she will have a child when no man has touched her, jesus will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, the newborn speaks, god creates by saying to a thing 'be' and it is (kun fa-yakun).

Only in Lot's old woman; Jonah and the fish: The fish casts the prophet onto a barren shore while he is sick; Jonah ran away (abaqa, as a runaway slave) to the laden ship; Had Jonah not been among those who glorify God he would have stayed in the fish's belly until the Day of Resurrection; Jonah is sent to a hundred thousand or more; they believe and are granted enjoyment for a while; The hearers pass by the ruins of Lot's people morning and night; Nineveh has more than 120,000 people who do not know their right hand from their left; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; The city to which Jonah is sent believes and is spared [divergence between the texts]; Jonah flees by ship [divergence between the texts]; Sailors cast lots to learn on whose account the disaster has come, and the lot falls on the prophet; Sailors cast lots to learn on whose account the disaster has come, and the lot falls on the prophet [divergence between the texts]; God makes a plant (qiqayon, gourd or castor) grow overnight to shade the prophet; and 4 more.

Only in Do you have a book or oaths binding God?; the shin laid bare; the companion of the fish; the evil eye: Do not be like the companion of the fish (sahib al-hut, Jonah) who cried out while choking with grief; God leads the deniers on step by step (istidraj) from where they do not know, and grants them respite; his plan is firm; Had not grace from his Lord reached him he would have been cast onto the barren shore blameworthy; but his Lord chose him and made him righteous; On the day when the shin is laid bare (yukshafu 'an saq) and they are called to prostrate but cannot; The unbelievers almost make the prophet slip with their (evil) eyes when they hear the reminder; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; At God's command the fish vomits the prophet onto dry land [divergence between the texts]; 'Are your unbelievers better than those, or have you an immunity (bara'a) in the scriptures (zubur)?'; The prophet is bitterly angry that God has spared the sinners; The prophet is bitterly angry that God has spared the sinners [divergence between the texts]; The word of God comes to the prophet a second time with the same commission; No messenger came to earlier peoples without being called 'a sorcerer or a madman', as if they had bequeathed the charge to one another; and 3 more.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Did they create the heavens and earth?; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; Dream of a ladder or stairway reaching heaven with angels ascending and descending; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; A ladder (sullam / sullām) reaching from earth to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; and 9 more.

title: The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue) ↔ The code of commandments (Surah 17:22-39)
summary: These two units share 6 motifs: do not kill your children for fear of poverty; god provides for them and you, honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts], guardians must keep orphans' property intact and hand it over when they come of age, the ten commandments (decalogue)….

title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)
summary: These two units share 5 motifs: the expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity, god commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do, the devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised, the devil (iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man….

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 17 more.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay (weight 6.3); The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 34.4.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 16 more.

Only in Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72): Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray; On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam); God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children; Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea; Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [contrast between the texts]; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [divergence between the texts]; God honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea and preferred them above much of creation; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol.

ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَآءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَآءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّٰظِرِينَ

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ

وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ

وَإِذْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ

وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنجَىٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ
إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعًا يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِىِّ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَٰظِرِينَ إِنَىٰهُ وَلَٰكِنْ إِذَا دُعِيتُمْ فَٱدْخُلُوا۟ فَإِذَا طَعِمْتُمْ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ وَلَا مُسْتَـْٔنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِى ٱلنَّبِىَّ فَيَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ وَإِذَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَٰعًا فَسْـَٔلُوهُنَّ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَطْهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمْ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّ وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُؤْذُوا۟ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَن تَنكِحُوٓا۟ أَزْوَٰجَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمًا
فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسْتَحْيُوا۟ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ

title: Who are the Quran's Sabians?
summary: The Quran names the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾūn) beside Jews and Christians. Candidates include the Mandaeans, the pagans of Harran, and Elchasaite baptists.

passages.text: (2:62) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (5:69) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـُٔونَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (22:17) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ

title: Sargon and Moses: the infant in the sealed basket
summary: The Neo-Assyrian Sargon Birth Legend has a baby placed in a reed basket sealed with bitumen, set on the river, and raised by a water-drawer. Exodus 2 and the Quran's Moses (into al-yamm) share the motif.

passages.note: papyrus basket daubed with bitumen and pitch
passages.text: (2:1) וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִ֖ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית לֵוִ֑י וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת בַּת לֵוִֽי (2:2) וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים (2:3) וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר (2:4) וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב אֲחֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה מַה יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ (2:5) וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ (2:6) וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה (2:7) וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל בַּת פַּרְעֹה֒ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת וְתֵינִ֥ק לָ֖ךְ אֶת הַיָּֽלֶד (2:8) וַתֹּֽאמֶר לָ֥הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵ֑כִי וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ הָֽעַלְמָ֔ה וַתִּקְרָ֖א אֶת אֵ֥ם הַיָּֽלֶד (2:9) וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ (2:10) וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ

passages.text: (20:38) إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ (20:39) أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ (28:7) وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ (28:8) فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ (28:9) وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (28:10) وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (28:11) وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (28:12) وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ (28:13) فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

The bitumen sealing is a specific shared detail between Sargon and Exodus.

title: Whoever saves one life
summary: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 teaches that destroying one life is like destroying a world, and saving one is like saving a world. Quran 5:32 states the same principle as decreed for the Children of Israel.

passages.text: مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًۢا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحْيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنْهُم بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ

evidence.text: The Quran explicitly frames it as a precept for the Children of Israel.
Mishnah manuscripts differ: some read 'a single life', others 'a single life of Israel'. Compare which reading the Quran matches.

title: Dara Shikoh's Upanishads reach Schopenhauer
summary: Dara Shikoh translated 50 Upanishads into Persian as the Sirr-i Akbar (1657). Anquetil-Duperron's Latin version (Oupnek'hat, 1801–02) is how Schopenhauer read them.

passages.ref: Dara Shikoh, Sirr-i Akbar (1657); Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (1655)

evidence.text: Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn ('the meeting of the two seas') takes its title from Quran 18:60.

title: Seven Sleepers and the People of the Cave
summary: Youths fleeing persecution sleep in a cave for centuries and wake to a changed world. Told in Syriac (Jacob of Serugh), Greek, and Latin sources, and in Quran 18:9–26.

passages.ref: Jacob of Serugh, homily on the Sleepers of Ephesus
Gregory of Tours, Passio septem dormientium

passages.text_omitted: longer than 12 verses; read it in the source

evidence.text: The Quran's debate over how many sleepers there were (18:22) suggests the audience knew competing versions.

title: tannūr: the oven that boiled at the Flood
summary: Akkadian tinūru (oven) reached Aramaic, Hebrew, and Arabic. In the Quran's Noah narrative the sign of the Flood is that the tannūr boiled over.

passages.note: and the oven boiled (fāra al-tannūr)
passages.text: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

evidence.text: The loan chain is established. The motif link (a hot or boiling flood) is the lead to investigate.

title: Plotinus as the 'Theology of Aristotle'
summary: An Arabic paraphrase of Plotinus' Enneads IV–VI circulated as the 'Theology of Aristotle' (al-Kindi's circle, 9th c.) and shaped Islamic Neoplatonism.

title: Ancient treaty form and Deuteronomy's covenant
summary: Deuteronomy follows the structure of ancient Near Eastern vassal treaties: preamble, history, stipulations, deposit, witnesses, curses and blessings.

evidence.text: Mendenhall (1954) argued for the Hittite model. Many scholars now consider Neo-Assyrian treaties the closer parallel. Which source is closer is the open question.

title: al-yamm: the sea word reserved for Moses
summary: The Quran's usual word for sea is bahr, but al-yamm appears 8 times across 4 surahs, always in the Moses/Pharaoh narrative. It is the Semitic sea word shared with Hebrew yam, Ugaritic Yam, and Mandaic yama, and borrowed into New Kingdom Egyptian.

lexical.gloss: Sea, the sea god opposed to Baal

passages.note: Pharaoh's people drowned in the yamm
passages.text: فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُوا۟ عَنْهَا غَٰفِلِينَ

passages.note: Infant Moses cast into the yamm (two occurrences)
passages.text: أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ

passages.note: Pharaoh's army overwhelmed
passages.text: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ

passages.note: The golden calf scattered into the yamm
passages.text: قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا

passages.note: Moses' mother told to cast him into the yamm
passages.text: وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

passages.note: Pharaoh and his army cast into the yamm
passages.text: فَأَخَذْنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

passages.note: Pharaoh and his army cast into the yamm
passages.text: فَأَخَذْنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ

passages.note: Pharaoh's officers drowned in yam suf
passages.text: מַרְכְּבֹ֥ת פַּרְעֹ֛ה וְחֵיל֖וֹ יָרָ֣ה בַיָּ֑ם וּמִבְחַ֥ר שָֽׁלִשָׁ֖יו טֻבְּע֥וּ בְיַם סֽוּף

evidence.text: 8 occurrences of the lemma, verified with the Quran word concordance (root ي م م); the other root hits are the unrelated verb tayammum (2:267, 4:43, 5:6).
Dispersion: 4 surahs (7, 20, 28, 51), 1 narrative. Concentrated in one story while spread across the text.
Synonym-choice skew: bahr is the general word for sea elsewhere in the Quran.
Egyptian ym is a Semitic loanword, so this is shared Semitic vocabulary fitting the Egyptian setting, not an Egyptian borrowing into Arabic.
